checks.note: Statement excerpt, proposition (FY25 $32.3B + FY26 $74.4B), conditions, axis and outcome are fine. Limitations match the packet: the SEC filing returned 403. Fails on the citation: e1's published excerpt is cut to "GPUs and CPUs". That drops the part the rationale relies on: "roughly two thirds of our capex was for short-lived assets". Readers can't see from the quote that this is about spending. Publish the full exact sentence. Publisher, dates, relation and locator are correct.

The excerpt is verbatim. The proposition keeps 'for the most part', 'willingly or otherwise' and 'more effective', and causal is a fair kind. The evidence supports the rationale: e1 says one Abilene building is operational; e2 says seven buildings are online and the site will reach 30; e3 says Rainier spans multiple data centers. It is balanced in both directions and doesn't claim the stated gaps are filled. The limitations are fair. Citations match the frozen items. The causal_assessment axis, unresolved outcome and not_applicable horizon match the agreed assessment.

overclaims: A purchaser's reported shortage provides countervailing context but cannot rule out eventual overbuilding.
checks.note: Excerpt, proposition, 'eventually' horizon, open_horizon and unresolved outcome are fine. Two problems. (1) e2 is Microsoft, a cloud provider, saying customer demand exceeds its available capacity. Calling it 'a purchaser's reported shortage' misdescribes who is short of what. (2) The published excerpts are cut down too far: e1 'GPU utilization' leaves out the 5% figure the rationale relies on, and e2 'exceed available capacity.' leaves out 'Customer demand continues to'. Publish the full exact sentences. Dates, publishers and relations are correct.
